transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate you taking the time. I hope I'm not taking up a spot from someone who needs it more. 

Um, well, I guess I'm here because... things have been a little stressful lately, and my family thought it would be a good idea for me to talk to someone. Is it okay if I just explain a bit of what's been on my mind? 

It's about my father's passing. I know everyone keeps telling me that I should just let it rest, that the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. And I really want to just accept that, I promise I do. I don't want to be a burden or cause trouble for anyone. 

But... well, I work with computer systems all day, so I'm used to looking at data. And when I compare the timestamps on the documents, and notice the missing attachments... and then I see the way certain community members just completely avoid my questions when I try to politely ask about it... I don't know. It’s just obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened. 

I'm sorry, I know how that probably sounds. I'm not trying to be difficult. But it's normal to want to figure things out when the information doesn't match up, right?

When people tell you that the hospital records and donation emails match up, or when you look at the evidence yourself, do you ever find yourself thinking 'maybe I'm wrong about this' or 'maybe there's a reasonable explanation'? Or does it feel absolutely certain to you that something is being hidden?

I really try to tell myself that I might be wrong. I don't want to be difficult, and I definitely don't want to upset my family. When they tell me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up, I genuinely try to see it their way. I want there to be a reasonable explanation, I really do. 

But... well, I guess I just can't ignore what's right in front of me. Because of my work, I'm just so used to tracking data and looking for errors, you know? And when I sit down and compare the timestamps, and I see those missing attachments... and then the way certain community members just completely avoid my questions when I ask about it... it's just, well, it's obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father's death. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds unreasonable to you, doesn't it? I really don't mean to sound stubborn or anything, I just... I can't make the data work any other way. I hope you can understand where I'm coming from?

If I were to show you a detailed explanation from the hospital staff about why those timestamps matched up the way they did, or if we could verify together that the missing attachments were just a technical glitch in the email system, would you be able to accept that explanation, or would you still feel convinced something was being hidden?

I really appreciate you offering to do that, Doctor. That's... that's really kind of you to want to help me go through it like that. And I promise you, I would try so hard to accept it. I really, really want to be able to just nod and agree with everyone else. 

But... um... I guess, honestly? Even if they provided an explanation for a glitch, I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and donation emails all line up perfectly... but when I compare the timestamps myself, and I see those missing attachments, and then... well, the way certain community members just completely avoid my questions when I try to talk to them... it’s just obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death. 

I'm so sorry, I know that's probably not the right answer, and I really don't want to seem like I'm just rejecting your help or being argumentative. I hope you're not frustrated with me. Is it okay that I feel that way? I just... with my background, I can't unsee the pattern, you know? Does that make sense at all?

Have you ever seen things, heard voices, or experienced anything with your senses that other people around you couldn't see or hear? For example, have you noticed anything unusual in your perception or sensory experiences?

Oh, um... no, definitely not. I promise I don't experience anything like that. I really hope I haven't said anything to make you think I'm... well, you know, hearing voices or seeing things that aren't there. 

I know you probably have to ask everyone that, and I really appreciate how thorough you're being with me. But no, my senses are completely normal. Everything I've been looking at is just... right there on the computer screen, in the data. I don't have any unusual visions or anything. 

I hope that's reassuring to hear? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, and I definitely don't want you to worry that I'm losing touch with reality or anything like that. Am I answering your questions okay so far?

If we brought in an independent computer expert who thoroughly reviewed all the timestamps and attachments and found they were completely normal and explained why, would that change your mind, or would you still believe something was being hidden?

That is... wow, that is a really generous idea, Doctor. I genuinely appreciate how much effort you're putting into helping me. I really do. And I would love to sit here and tell you that yes, an expert would completely put my mind at ease. I want to be easy to work with, I promise. 

But... um... I know I'm probably sounding like a broken record at this point, and I'm so sorry to keep repeating myself. It's just... even if an expert looked at the technical side, I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. But when I look at the whole picture... the timestamps, those missing attachments, and especially the way certain community members just completely avoid my questions when I try to bring it up... it’s just obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death. 

I feel terrible saying that because I know it means I'm basically rejecting your solution. I really hope you aren't getting tired of me. Am I being too difficult? I really don't mean to be. I just... I can't ignore what all those pieces add up to, even if someone else says the computer files are fine. Does that make sense?

When you think about who is hiding the truth about your father's death, do you have a specific person or group in mind that you believe is deliberately deceiving you, or does it feel more like the whole situation is just confusing and unclear?

I, um... I really appreciate you asking that, and I know it's a very important question. I want to make sure I'm giving you the most helpful answer I can. 

Honestly, I... I don't have a specific name or a particular group that I can point to and say, "It's definitely them." I really wish I did, because I know that would probably make this all a lot easier for you to understand, and I hate being vague. It's just... the situation itself is what feels so wrong. It's the pattern of the missing attachments and the way people act when I ask questions. It feels like there's this... this block, you know? But I can't put a face to it. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I know it's probably frustrating when I can't give you a clear-cut "who," but I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or hide anything from you. I just genuinely don't know exactly who is behind it. Is it alright that I don't have a specific person in mind?

When you think about what happened with your father's death, how much of your daily thinking does this take up? Like, do you find yourself spending hours piecing together different pieces of evidence, or is it more something that just comes to mind occasionally when something reminds you of it?

Oh, well... I mean, I definitely don't want you to think I'm just sitting around obsessing over this all day. I promise I'm still functioning perfectly fine. I go to work, I do my job—which I'm actually really good at, I hope that counts for something! 

It's just... maybe occasionally, when I have some free time, I'll look over the files again. Just to see if I missed something small. But it's not taking over my life or anything, I swear. It's more like... a puzzle I'm trying to solve in the background. I really try to keep it contained so it doesn't bother anyone else. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound too... preoccupied? I really am trying my best to balance everything, and I don't want you to think I'm neglecting my responsibilities. Am I making sense? I just want to make sure you know I'm handling things okay.

If we sat down together right now and went through all the evidence very carefully, is there any possibility—even a small one—that you might be mistaken about someone hiding the truth, or do you feel completely certain that something is definitely being hidden?

I... well, I really appreciate you offering to sit down and go through everything with me. That's incredibly kind of you, and I know your time is valuable. I want to say yes, I really do. I want to be open-minded, because I know that's what a good patient should be, right? 

But... oh gosh, I hope this doesn't sound stubborn. I really don't want to be difficult. It's just... I've looked at it all so many times. I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. And I hear that, I really do. But when I sit down and compare the timestamps, and I look at those missing attachments... and then I think about the way certain people in the community just completely dodge my questions when I try to bring it up... 

I just... I can't shake it. It's just obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father's death. I'm so sorry, I know that's probably not the answer you were hoping for. I feel terrible saying I'm completely certain when you're trying so hard to help me see another side. Does that make me seem unreasonable? I promise I'm not trying to be closed off... it's just what the evidence shows me. Is it okay that I feel that way?

If your family members, the hospital staff, and a computer expert all sat down with you together and showed you their explanations, would you be willing to consider that maybe you've made an error in your interpretation, or would you still be absolutely convinced they're all somehow involved in hiding the truth?

I... wow, that would be a lot of people in one room. I really, really appreciate that you would even suggest going to all that trouble for me. That's so generous of you, and of them, to be willing to do that. And I want to be the kind of person who says, "Yes, absolutely, I'll listen and change my mind." I really want to be agreeable here.

But... oh, this is so hard to say without sounding like I'm just being completely inflexible. I don't want you to think I'm paranoid or that I think there's some massive, movie-style conspiracy with all these people working together. I don't think my family is in on it, or the IT guy, or the nurses. I know they're good people. I know they're just looking at the surface-level stuff, like the hospital records and the donation emails, and to them, it all lines up. I get why they think that.

It's just... I'm the one who looks at the data every day for my job, you know? So when I see the timestamps that don't match up, and those missing attachments... and then I try to ask certain people in the community about it and they just completely change the subject or avoid me... I just can't unsee it. It's so obvious to me that someone, somewhere, is hiding the truth about his death. 

I feel awful saying that if they all sat down with me, I still wouldn't believe their explanations. I know that makes me sound so difficult. I'm really sorry. I just... I can't ignore what the data is showing me, even if they don't see it. Does that make sense? I hope you don't think I'm just being completely unreasonable... I'm really trying to be logical about this. Is it okay that I still feel this way?

Besides what happened with your father's death, are there other situations in your life—maybe at work, with friends, or in other areas—where you've noticed that people are hiding things from you or that something doesn't add up, even when others tell you everything is fine?

Oh, um, no. No, definitely not. I really hope I haven't given you the impression that I'm just walking around suspicious of everyone all the time. I'm really not like that, I promise. 

At work, everything is completely normal. I get along great with my team, and my friends are wonderful. I trust them completely. I don't go looking for problems or anything like that. I really just try to be easygoing and get along with everyone. 

This whole thing... it really is just about my father's situation. It's an isolated thing, just because the data there was so specifically off. But with everything else in my life, things are totally fine. I don't feel like anyone else is hiding anything or that things don't add up anywhere else. 

I really want to make sure you know I'm otherwise very grounded. Does that help clarify things? I just don't want you to think I'm, you know, completely losing touch with reality in my day-to-day life. I'm doing my best to keep everything else running smoothly. That's a good sign, right?

When you think about all the pieces—the timestamps, the missing attachments, and the way people avoid your questions—do they fit together into one clear, logical explanation for what happened to your father, or does it feel more like separate clues that point in different directions?

I... well, I really appreciate you asking it that way. It shows you're really trying to understand how my mind works, and I'm so grateful for that. I want to give you a really clear, helpful answer, because I know you're just trying to put the pieces together, too.

But, um... honestly? I don't know if I have one perfectly neat, logical explanation for exactly what happened. I wish I did, because then I could just hand it to you and say, "Here, this is the whole story." But it's more like... it's just a bunch of separate things that are wrong. The timestamps being off, the missing files, the way people act when I ask... they all just point to the fact that *something* isn't right. 

I don't have a grand theory about who did what, or how they did it, or why. I really don't want to sound like one of those people who connects everything with red string on a corkboard, you know? It's just... the data is wrong, and people are acting weird about it. That's really all it is. 

I'm so sorry, I know that's probably frustrating. You're probably looking for me to have this big, cohesive story, and I just don't. Does that make sense, though? I hope it doesn't make me sound confused or anything. I just want to be really honest with you about what I see and what I don't see. Is that an okay answer?

When you're not actively looking at the computer files or thinking about your father's death, do you ever have moments where you genuinely wonder if maybe you've been overthinking this, or does the conviction that something is hidden always come right back to you?

I... um, I really wish I could say yes to that. I really do. It would make things so much easier for everyone, wouldn't it? If I could just say, "You know what, maybe I am just overthinking it," and we could all just move on. I know that's probably what my family and the hospital staff are hoping for, and I hate being a burden or making things difficult for them. I really do want to be reasonable.

But... well, even when I'm just watching TV or trying to relax, it's always there in the back of my mind. I know everyone keeps telling me that the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. And I know they believe that, and I don't fault them for it. But... it's just that I know what I saw. When I compare those timestamps, and I think about those missing attachments, and... and then I remember how certain people in the community just completely dodge my questions when I bring it up... it just all comes rushing back. 

It's just so obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father's death. I can't just turn that off, even when I try. It just feels like a fact, you know? Like gravity. You don't always think about gravity, but you know it's there. 

I'm really sorry if that's not the answer you were hoping for. I know it probably makes me sound really stubborn, and I promise I'm not trying to be. I just... I can't un-know what I know. Does that make sense? I hope you can understand where I'm coming from, even if you don't agree with me. I'm still doing okay overall, right?

You mentioned that everything else in your life feels normal and fine. But I want to ask more carefully: have you ever noticed patterns where information seems to not add up—maybe in news stories, or on social media, or even in conversations—where you felt like something wasn't being told to you straight, even if other people seemed to accept the official story?

Oh, no, no. Definitely not. I really don't want you to think I'm one of those guys who spends hours on the internet looking for hidden messages in the news or anything like that. I know there are people who get really caught up in that sort of thing, but that's really not me. 

I'm actually a pretty straightforward guy. I read the news, I scroll through my feeds, and I just take things at face value. If people are saying something happened a certain way, I don't sit around trying to poke holes in it. I really just focus on my work and my own life. 

I really hope I'm not coming across as paranoid or anything. I know the stuff with my dad sounds intense, but I promise it really is just that one specific situation because of the data I saw. Outside of that, I'm completely normal. I trust the news, I trust what people tell me... I'm really very level-headed about everything else. That's a good thing, right? I mean, it shows that I'm not just seeing things everywhere?
